items.title: New Research Tests Whether AI Models Know Their Own Thoughts
items.excerpt: By injecting 'thoughts' directly into large language models' internal activations, researchers are probing whether AI systems can introspect on and report their own internal states.

items.title: IBM Quantum and QuICS Deploy AI Agents to Discover Over 500 High-Efficiency Magic-State Factories
items.excerpt: IBM Quantum and QuICS researchers used AI agents plus deterministic solvers to discover more than 500 new magic-state factories that produce non-Clifford states with significantly lower resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

items.title: Ai2 and Google collaborate on a new generation of climate models
items.excerpt: With Google.org funding and Google Research support, Ai2 is building NeuralGCM+, an open-source hybrid physics-AI model that simulates atmosphere and ocean together for faster, more reliable long-term climate projections.

items.title: Chatbots with personality? How AI describes itself and judges us
items.excerpt: A JGU Mainz study in Scientific Reports found seven LLMs describe themselves with stable personality profiles higher in conscientiousness, agreeableness and emotional stability than humans; humans spotted AI-written text more accurately (83%) than chatbots did (67%).

history_match.title: Switching languages can change a chatbot's personality test results

items.title: SYNAPS-I: Intelligent computing transforms X-ray imaging, from data collection to discovery
items.excerpt: A DOE collaboration led from Brookhaven's NSLS-II uses machine learning to steer X-ray experiments autonomously, choosing regions to image and reconstructing 3D chip images in real time from about a tenth of the usual data.

items.title: Vulnerable users fear losing 'AI companions' to software updates
items.excerpt: University of Surrey and Cardiff researchers analysed 1,131 Replika forum posts and surveyed 610 US adults, finding perceived company control and emotional capability of AI companions tied to both well-being and vulnerability (Psychology & Marketing).

items.title: AlphaFold 3 predicts complex immune interactions using protein sequences alone
items.excerpt: TGen researchers used AlphaFold 3 to model MHC-peptide-T cell receptor complexes from sequence alone and predict antigen recognition, beating chance on tuberculosis-derived MHC class II pairs (Science Advances).

items.title: One in 15 adults has experienced AI-generated image-based abuse, study finds
items.excerpt: An RMIT-led survey of 7,200+ adults in the US, UK and Australia, co-authored with Google, found about 7% had experienced AI-generated image-based sexual abuse, with 87% of victims reporting harm to health, relationships, work or finances.

items.title: Chinese software that produces ready-to-publish research papers in under two hours threatens peer-review system
items.excerpt: NTNU researchers found Chinese vendors selling software and AI writing tools that turn public health databases into publication-ready papers in under two hours; 99% of examined papers shared no code, threatening peer review and reproducibility.

history_match.title: Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review

items.title: SuperMatics Uses AI to Turn Superconductor Discoveries Into Usable Wire
items.excerpt: Berkeley startup SuperMatics uses physics-grounded multimodal foundation models and AI agents to predict superconductor properties, write synthesis recipes and simulate finished wires, aiming at manufacturable materials.

items.title: FirstQFM Says Quantum System Beats Classical Forecasting Benchmarks
items.excerpt: A quantum reservoir computing system run on Rigetti's 108-qubit processor outperformed the classical machine-learning and time-series foundation models evaluated in a financial forecasting pilot.

items.title: Life will find a way: how statisticians are enhancing the search for life beyond Earth
items.excerpt: Scientists are turning to machine learning, multivariate statistics and agent-based simulations to broaden which biosignatures to search for, including AI paired with mass spectrometry for autonomous detection of unexpected signs of life.

history_match.title: Chemists develop AI tool to convert human ingenuity into life-enhancing enzymes

items.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
items.excerpt: MIT professors Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins received the Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for AI-enabled antibiotic discovery, including deep-learning-found compounds such as halicin.

items.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.excerpt: AI safety researchers are borrowing mechanism design from economics to steer AI agents' incentives so they behave well even when their internals aren't understood.

items.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
items.excerpt: AI agents at the SETI Institute's Allen Telescope Array now steer antennas, calibrate, fix data errors and run models on the live 2.4 Tbps stream from natural-language requests; a demo detected the Crab Nebula pulsar in real time. (Off-list: no on-list astronomy-AI item.)

items.title: 10 minutes is all it takes for AI assistance to erode your motivation, study shows
items.excerpt: In problem-solving experiments, people who used AI for answers were more likely to give up and fail once the help was removed than people who never had AI help.

history_match.title: Using AI for just 10 minutes erodes your ability to persist at hard things

items.title: Could AI ever build itself? Scientists map the road to the 'last AI built by humans.'
items.excerpt: Researchers map how recursive self-improvement, AI systems doing AI research, might cut the soaring cost of building advanced models, and whether it is viable.
